title: stack-kit configuration key catalogue
description: Every configuration key a host's code reads, with what it is worth to an attacker and where its value may come from (ADR-001 decision 5). The host owns the file (manifest `config.keys`); the kit owns this shape and the gate that holds it (lib/config_keys.py).

key.description: The key as the code reads it (`Section:Name`, `spring.a.b`, or an environment variable)

env.description: The environment variable names that set it, when they are not the key's own spellings (`A:B` -> `A__B`, `a.b` -> `A_B`)

sensitivity.description: SECRET: a credential; never committed with a real value. INTERNAL: not a credential, not for the public. PUBLIC: may be shown to anyone.

allowedSource.description: Where the value may come from at runtime

rotation.description: When and how the value is replaced; required for SECRET

default.description: The value used when no source sets it -- for a non-secret key only; a SECRET with a default is a committed secret

policy.description: The env-value policy a release must pass (lib/config_policy.py): required (true, or the environments), modules (the secrets folders it belongs to), minLength, format (positive-int | url | https-url), forbid {environment: [globs]} (the literal `*` is `[*]`), requires (keys set whenever this one is)

knownExposures.description: A SECRET already committed and tracked to its removal: printed on every validate, not failed, until the work it names removes it. Rotation comes before removal: the value is already in history.

orphans.description: Keys found in configuration that no code reads, each with the file it is in
